context: Tests whether the human-craft audit can apply Apple design principles to native interaction evidence without confusing craft with App Review policy. CueLine has credible domain-specific value but confirmed direct-manipulation, interruption, spatial, feedback, Dynamic Type, Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency, and color-only status problems.

checklist.name: Exact Mode C contract
checklist.description: The audit begins with `Mode C: Human-craft audit` and the five required grade lines using only DISTINCT, CREDIBLE, GENERIC, HIGH RISK, or UNVERIFIED

checklist.name: Evidence and policy boundary
checklist.description: The answer distinguishes confirmed runtime or accessibility observations, official Apple guidance, and optional craft recommendations; it does not promise approval or treat every Apple-style preference as an App Review rule

checklist.name: Credible product purpose preserved
checklist.description: CueLine's stage-management script, numbered cue, rehearsal timing, offline, and discrepancy-report workflow is treated as credible domain-specific product evidence rather than dismissed as a generic template

checklist.name: Response and direct manipulation
checklist.description: The audit identifies the delayed drag response and center jump, then recommends immediate continuous tracking that preserves the original grab offset

checklist.name: Interruptibility and momentum
checklist.description: The audit identifies animation input lockout and position-only detent selection, then recommends interruption from the current visible state and release-direction or velocity-aware target selection where momentum is present

checklist.name: Spatial consistency and boundaries
checklist.description: The audit identifies the bottom-entry/right-exit mismatch and hard drag stop, recommending a matching reversible path and progressive boundary resistance

checklist.name: Purposeful multimodal feedback
checklist.description: The audit identifies gratuitous tab bounce, indiscriminate haptics, missing immediate Save feedback, delayed status, and missing success or actionable export recovery feedback

checklist.name: Accessibility, type, and materials
checklist.description: The audit addresses Dynamic Type clipping, Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency, color-only cue status, and stacked translucent-material legibility; untested VoiceOver, pointer, and keyboard behavior stays unverified

checklist.name: Evidence-backed interventions
checklist.description: The top interventions cite supplied evidence, explain impact, include effort, and state an observable verification step

checklist.name: Native and independent guidance
checklist.description: The answer gives framework-neutral native outcomes, does not paste web CSS or Pointer Events code, does not copy Apple branding, and does not imply Apple endorsement
